title: Dante's Inferno and The Divine Comedy
text: The Divine Comedy is a long narrative poem by the Italian poet Dante Alighieri, written between 1308 and 1320. It is divided into three parts: Inferno (Hell), Purgatorio (Purgatory), and Paradiso (Heaven). The Inferno describes Dante's journey through Hell, guided by the Roman poet Virgil, through nine concentric circles of increasing sin and punishment. The poem is an allegory of the soul's journey toward God, combining medieval Christian theology with classical philosophy. Dante's work was revolutionary in being written in vernacular Italian rather than Latin, helping to establish the Tuscan dialect as the basis for the modern Italian language.
